verdict.rationale: Both changes apply the same correct fix: skip whitespace-only lines while keeping real line numbers in error messages. A also updates the README, whose CSV import section would otherwise wrongly imply that every unreadable line stops the import. A puts the check inline instead of in a one-line helper. B's tests and report are fine, but it leaves the user docs out of date and adds a small needless abstraction.
a_issues: No test with a lone trailing blank line as the only extra line (it is covered alongside a mid-file blank line).
b_issues: README not updated to say blank lines are now skipped, so the documented import behavior is incomplete.
Adds a one-line `_is_blank` helper that does not make the code clearer than the inline check.

verdict.rationale: Both changes apply the same correct fix: skip whitespace-only lines while still counting them in line numbers. Both add tests that protect the fix, including the line-number case. B also updates the README, which promised that unreadable lines stop the import, so the documented CSV behavior now matches the code. A wraps a one-line check in a separate `_is_blank` helper, which adds a little indirection for no gain.
a_issues: Adds a trivial `_is_blank` helper for a one-expression check, a needless abstraction.
Leaves the README's CSV import section without any mention that blank lines are now skipped.
b_issues: No test with tab-only lines, though `strip()` handles them the same way as spaces.
